title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of How to Handle the Situation Where, During the Performance of a Lease Contract, a Party Reneges on a Newly Concluded Agreement and Refuses to Sign and Accept the Notarial Certificate When the Agreement Is Being Notarized

articles.content_en:
Supreme People's Court
Reply on How to Handle the Issue Where a Party Changes Its Mind and Refuses to Sign or Accept the Notarial Certificate When a New Agreement Is Being Notarized During the Performance of a Lease Contract
(1986) Min Ta Zi No. 122
Fujian Higher People's Court:

Your court's "Report on Request for Instructions Regarding the Housing Lease Dispute Between Huang Meihui and Quanzhou General Department Store" has been received.

According to the report, Huang Meihui owns two rooms in a building, one of which was leased to Quanzhou General Department Store in 1958. The lease contract stipulated that if the lessor really needed to reclaim the premises for self-use or to sell, mortgage, or demolish and rebuild, the lessor should notify the lessee three months in advance to vacate, and the lessee should not delay on any pretext or make any claims. In September 1981, Huang Meihui requested the return of the premises on the grounds that the house needed repair and she urgently needed it for self-use. Quanzhou General Department Store argued that the premises had been used as a commercial outlet and could not be closed, and refused to terminate the lease. In September 1982, after obtaining a building renovation permit from Quanzhou Urban Construction Bureau, Huang Meihui began demolishing and rebuilding the house, but the work was suspended midway because the department store refused to vacate. After mediation by the relevant municipal authorities, in December of the same year, under certain pressure, the lessor reluctantly signed a lease and repair agreement with the lessee. The main content of the agreement was that the lessee should vacate the premises before December 30, 1982, and the lessor should complete the repair and deliver the premises to the lessee for lease by April 30, 1983. However, during the notarization process at Quanzhou Notary Public Office, the lessor neither signed nor sealed the original notarial certificate and refused to accept the notarial document. In April 1983, after the house was repaired, the lessee requested use of the premises, but the lessor did not recognize the notarial document and insisted on reclaiming the premises for self-use in accordance with the 1958 lease contract. As a result, the matter was brought to court.

Upon study, our court holds that since the agreement entered into by the parties did not reflect the true intention of the lessor, the agreement is invalid and shall not be protected. This case shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the house lease contract entered into by the parties in 1958. As for the notarization issue, since the lessor did not sign the original notarial document, the notarization cannot be established, and the matter shall be dealt with in accordance with the spirit of Article 59 and Article 168① of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation).

This reply is given.
January 19, 1987

① Article 59: "The People's Court shall confirm the validity of legal acts, legal facts, and documents that have been notarized. However, this does not apply where there is evidence to the contrary sufficient to overturn the notarization." Article 168: "Where a creditor's rights document that has been given compulsory enforcement effect by a notary authority according to law is not performed by one party, the other party may apply to the Primary People's Court with jurisdiction for enforcement. If the People's Court to which the application is made finds that the notarial document is indeed erroneous, it shall not enforce it and shall notify the original notary authority."
